# Preface {.unnumbered}

Most R packages that fit a statistical model contain their own code for
probability distributions, link functions and optimization. This code is
usually written as internal helper functions, and it serves only the model
that the package fits. For example, a package may contain a Gamma density
with its score, a logit link with its derivative, and a Newton iteration
with its own stopping rule. The next package writes all of this again.
Each author usually writes the derivatives up to the order that their own model
needs, and no further. Because the code is internal, other packages
cannot reuse it or extend it.

`statmodels7` is a toolkit in which each of these pieces is written only
once. A distribution is an object that contains its density and all the
derivatives that a fitting routine may need, up to the fourth order and
with respect to the unconstrained parameters. A link function contains its
derivatives in both directions. An optimizer is an object with an explicit
stopping rule. Model terms, penalties and bases are objects too. The
function `statmod()` builds a model from these pieces. A user can write a
new piece, and `statmod()` accepts it in the same way as a piece that comes
with the toolkit.

This book is written first for readers who want to fit models with the
toolkit, and then for readers who want to extend it. In the first chapter
we fit one model to real data and read its output from the first line to
the last.
